# A template reached once, through a chain of {{template}} invocations, is
# mutated once and trimmed nowhere.
#
# "page" invokes "middle", which invokes "leaf". The checker that finds
# each invocation's dot follows it into the template it names, so it also
# sees the invocations written further down the chain. Only the ones
# written in a template count as its own; otherwise "leaf" would be listed
# as trimmed against the very call that mutated it.

muxt test-template-mutations --dry-run -v --seed 1
cmp stdout want.txt
! stdout trimmed

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "leaf"}}<p>{{.Title}}</p>{{end}}
{{define "middle"}}{{template "leaf" .}}{{end}}
{{define "page"}}{{template "middle" .}}{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Page struct {
	Title string
}

func Render(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "page", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestPage(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Page{Title: "hi"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "<p>hi</p>"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("page = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
-- want.txt --
